content: Statistical arbitrage/pairs trading pitfalls: cointegration relationships can change or disappear due to regime shifts; risk increases near regime-switching times. Without economic justification for comovement (shared base currency, commodity exposure, risk-sentiment regime), a historical correlation is coincidence and breaks under stress. Multiple-testing problem: with hundreds of pair combinations tested, a meaningful fraction will test as cointegrated purely by chance (e.g. ~30 of 595 combos by chance alone) -- must control for this when scanning many pairs. Engle-Granger two-step test is sensitive to variable ordering, so residual properties can differ depending on which series is regressed on which. Continuing to trade a pair whose cointegration has broken/flipped without re-testing periodically is a critical and common error.
